description: Fatigue evaluation (stress-life, strain-life, critical-plane stress- and strain-based, energy-based, rainflow cumulative damage, harmonic and random vibration fatigue, mean stress corrections and results) and rotordynamics (Solid Rotor, Fixed Frame, Beam Rotor features, bearings, foundations, seals, couplings, hydrodynamic bearings, Campbell/whirl/stability evaluation and waterfall studies). Type strings and parameter keys were confirmed in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models where Java is shown.

tools.name: Fatigue (study)
tools.description: Dedicated study step that post-processes a previously computed load cycle (Stationary load cases, parametric or time-dependent solutions, frequency sweeps or a random-vibration ROM) and evaluates the criteria defined in the Fatigue interface. In Values of Variables Not Solved For the method is Solution and the study with the load cycle is selected; All, From list or Manual picks the load events forming the cycle. Include geometric nonlinearity must match the load-cycle study.
tools.usage: Study > Fatigue. Java: model.study("std2").create("ftge", "Fatigue"); feature("ftge").set("usesol", "on"); set("notsolmethod", "sol"); set("notstudy", "std1"); set("notsolnum", "all") (keys confirmed in the stored study-step properties of the bracket_fatigue library model).

parameters.name: Values of variables not solved for
parameters.description: User controlled, Method = Solution, Study = load-cycle study, selection of load cases/time steps/parameters.

parameters.name: Include geometric nonlinearity
parameters.description: Must match the load-cycle simulation (important for large rotations).

parameters.name: Physics and Variables Selection
parameters.description: Only Fatigue interfaces solved; several Fatigue interfaces can be evaluated in one study.

tools.notes: A Stationary study with only the Fatigue interface selected is an older alternative with fewer options (always all steps).

tools.name: Stress-Life (Fatigue)
tools.description: High-cycle fatigue life from a stress-amplitude based curve: an S-N curve function (with optional stress factor k for surface/size effects), the Basquin model, or the four-parameter Approximate S-N curve (transition and endurance points). The stress measure is principal stress or signed von Mises (principal or hydrostatic sign), and the mean stress can be corrected with Gerber, Goodman or Soderberg. The result is the number of cycles to failure ftg.ctf, bounded by the cycle cutoff.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Life (domains, boundaries, edges, points). Java: physics().create("ftg", "Fatigue", "geom1"); physics("ftg").create("slif1", "StressLifeModel", 3); set("fatigueInputPhysics", "solid"); set("ftgLimit", "SNCurve" | "Basquin"); set("stress", "stressPrincipal" | "stressMisesPrincipal").

parameters.name: fatigueInputPhysics
parameters.description: Structural interface where the load cycle was computed (solid, shell, mbd, rotor...).

parameters.name: ftgLimit
parameters.description: SNCurve, Basquin or approximate S-N curve.

parameters.name: stress
parameters.description: stressPrincipal, stressMisesPrincipal or signed von Mises (hydrostatic).

parameters.name: ftgSNModification, lifeCurve
parameters.description: Stress factor modification and the S-N curve function.

parameters.name: Mean stress correction
parameters.description: None, Gerber, Goodman (ultimate strength) or Soderberg (yield stress).

tools.notes: Requires the Fatigue Module. For shells choose the through-thickness location (top/bottom). Application Library: Fatigue_Module/Stress_Life/bracket_fatigue and Multibody_Dynamics_Module/Automotive_and_Aerospace/engine_fatigue.

tools.name: Basquin and Approximate S-N Curve (Fatigue Models)
tools.description: Analytic stress-life relations used by Stress-Life, Random Vibration and finite-life Findley/Matake: Basquin sigma_a = sigma_f' (2N)^b with fatigue strength coefficient and exponent (and shear counterparts tau_f', b_gamma); the Approximate S-N curve is a piecewise log-linear curve through a transition point (S_t, N_t) and an endurance point (S_e, N_e). Parameters come from the fatigueStressBasquin material property group or are user defined.
tools.usage: Material > Add property group Basquin (fatigueStressBasquin: sigmaf_Basquin, b_Basquin, tauf_Basquin, bgamma_Basquin); Fatigue > Stress Life > Fatigue limit = Basquin | Approximate S-N curve.

parameters.name: sigmaf_Basquin, b_Basquin
parameters.description: Fatigue strength coefficient and exponent (axial).

parameters.name: tauf_Basquin, bgamma_Basquin
parameters.description: Shear fatigue strength coefficient and exponent (critical-plane finite life).

parameters.name: S_t, N_t, S_e, N_e
parameters.description: Approximate S-N curve transition and endurance points.

tools.notes: Basquin is the elastic part of the combined Basquin-Coffin-Manson strain-life equation.

tools.name: Strain-Life and Coffin-Manson (Fatigue)
tools.description: Low-cycle fatigue life from strain amplitude: an E-N curve function, Coffin-Manson (plastic/inelastic strain amplitude with fatigue ductility coefficient eps_f' and exponent c, driven by equivalent plastic, creep or viscoplastic strain or a user-defined inelastic strain), or combined Basquin and Coffin-Manson (total strain, with optional Morrow mean-stress correction). Results give the number of cycles to failure for thermo-mechanical fatigue of solder joints, eyeglass frames and components cycled into plasticity.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Strain Life. Java: physics("ftg").create("elif1", "StrainLifeModel", 2); set("ftgElifCrit", "CoffinManson" | "CombinedBAndCM"); set("strainTypeCM", "Creep" | "User"); material group fatigueStrainCoffinManson (epsilonf_CM, c_CM, gammaf_CM, cgamma_CM).

parameters.name: ftgElifCrit
parameters.description: E-N curve, CoffinManson or CombinedBAndCM.

parameters.name: strainTypeCM
parameters.description: Equivalent plastic/creep/viscoplastic strain or user-defined inelastic strain (with its integration order).

parameters.name: epsilonf_CM, c_CM
parameters.description: Fatigue ductility coefficient and exponent.

parameters.name: Mean stress correction
parameters.description: None or Morrow for the combined model.

tools.notes: Inelastic strains require the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module in the stress analysis.

tools.name: Findley (Stress-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Critical-plane high-cycle criterion: Delta_tau/2 + k*sigma_n,max = f, with the critical plane maximizing the left-hand side. It is the default multiaxial criterion for non-proportional loading of shafts, rims and contacts. The Limit factor evaluation gives a fatigue usage factor ftg.fus (ratio to f, below 1 means infinite life); the Finite life evaluation uses shear Basquin data to compute cycles to failure. The critical-plane search resolution Q and the shear range search (circumscribing circle or maximum distance) control accuracy and cost.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Based > Criterion = Findley. Java: physics("ftg").create("stre1", "StressBasedModel", 3); set("fatigueHCFMultiaxModel", "Findley"); material group fatigueStressFindley (k_Findley, f_Findley).

parameters.name: k_Findley, f_Findley
parameters.description: Normal stress sensitivity coefficient and limit factor.

parameters.name: Evaluation method
parameters.description: Limit factor (usage factor) or Finite life (tau_f', b_gamma, cycle cutoff).

parameters.name: Search resolution Q
parameters.description: Number of evaluation points for the critical plane (default 11).

parameters.name: Shear range search method
parameters.description: Circumscribing circle or Maximum distance.

tools.notes: k and f are fitted from two fatigue limits (e.g. tension and torsion). Compressive states giving negative values set fus to zero.

tools.name: Matake (Stress-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Critical-plane criterion closely related to Findley, but the critical plane is the one with maximum shear stress range and the maximum normal stress is taken on that plane: Delta_tau/2 + k*sigma_n,max = f. It also supports Limit factor (usage factor) and Finite life (shear Basquin) evaluation.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Based > Criterion = Matake. Java: set("fatigueHCFMultiaxModel", "Matake"); material group fatigueStressMatake (k_Matake, f_Matake).

parameters.name: k_Matake, f_Matake
parameters.description: Normal stress sensitivity coefficient and limit factor.

parameters.name: Evaluation method
parameters.description: Limit factor or Finite life.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ftg").feature("stre1").set("fatigueHCFMultiaxModel", "Matake");
// Application Library: Fatigue_Module/Verification_Examples/cylindrical_test_specimen (compares Findley, Matake, Normal stress)
tools.notes: Cheaper than Findley because the plane search is based on shear range only.

tools.name: Normal Stress Criterion (Stress-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: One-parameter critical-plane criterion that ignores shear: the plane with maximum normal stress range is critical and the usage factor is Delta_sigma_n/2 divided by the limit factor f. Suitable for brittle materials and uniaxial-dominated loading; not appropriate when mean stress matters (the limit must include mean stress effects).
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Based > Criterion = Normal stress. Java: set("fatigueHCFMultiaxModel", "NormalStress"); material group fatigueStressNormalStress (f_NormalStress).

parameters.name: f_NormalStress
parameters.description: Limit factor (tensile fatigue limit).

parameters.name: Search resolution Q
parameters.description: Critical-plane search resolution.

tools.notes: Results are the fatigue usage factor ftg.fus.

tools.name: Dang Van (Stress-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Mesoscopic multiaxial endurance criterion: tau_max(t) + a_DV*sigma_H(t) <= b_DV, where the microscopic shear stress is obtained after an elastic-shakedown correction (center of the smallest hypersphere enclosing the deviatoric load path). It is widely used for rolling contact, railway wheels and automotive components under complex non-proportional loading; the result is the usage factor ftg.fus.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Based > Criterion = Dang Van. Java: set("fatigueHCFMultiaxModel", "DangVan"); material group fatigueStressDangVan (a_DangVan, b_DangVan).

parameters.name: a_DangVan
parameters.description: Hydrostatic stress sensitivity coefficient alpha_DV.

parameters.name: b_DangVan
parameters.description: Limit factor beta_DV (shear endurance limit).

tools.notes: No critical-plane search settings are needed.

tools.name: Smith-Watson-Topper (Strain-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Critical-plane low-cycle criterion using the product of the maximum normal stress and the normal strain amplitude on a plane, sigma_n,max*Delta_eps/2 = sigma_f'^2/E (2N)^(2b) + sigma_f' eps_f' (2N)^(b+c), which accounts for mean stress. The load cycle can be a Full elastoplastic solution or an Elastic solution with notch assumption (elastic results corrected with a cyclic Ramberg-Osgood curve), and gives cycles to failure.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Strain Based > Criterion = Smith-Watson-Topper (SWT). Java: physics("ftg").create("stra1", "StrainBasedModel", 2); set("fatigueLCFType", "fatigueLCFPlastic" | "fatigueLCFElastic"); material groups fatigueStressBasquin, fatigueStrainCoffinManson, elastoplasticRambergOsgood (K_ROcyclic, n_ROcyclic).

parameters.name: fatigueLCFType
parameters.description: Full elastoplastic solution or elastic solution with notch assumption.

parameters.name: sigma_f', b, eps_f', c
parameters.description: Fatigue strength/ductility coefficients and exponents.

parameters.name: K_ROcyclic, n_ROcyclic
parameters.description: Cyclic Ramberg-Osgood data for the notch approximation.

tools.notes: SWT is best for materials failing by tensile cracking.

tools.name: Fatemi-Socie and Wang-Brown (Strain-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Shear-based critical-plane low-cycle criteria for materials that crack in shear. Fatemi-Socie uses the maximum shear strain amplitude amplified by the normal stress on that plane (k*sigma_n,max/sigma_ys), with shear fatigue data given explicitly or implied from tensile data. Wang-Brown combines maximum shear strain and normal strain excursion (normal strain sensitivity S) with optional Morrow mean-stress correction.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Strain Based > Criterion = Fatemi-Socie | Wang-Brown.

parameters.name: tau_f', b_gamma, gamma_f', c_gamma
parameters.description: Shear fatigue data (Fatemi-Socie, explicit) or implied from tensile data.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Normal stress sensitivity coefficient (Fatemi-Socie).

parameters.name: S
parameters.description: Normal strain sensitivity coefficient (Wang-Brown).

parameters.name: G / E, sigma_ys0, nu
parameters.description: Constitutive data needed by the chosen solution type.

tools.example:
Fatigue > Strain Based 1
Criterion: Fatemi-Socie, Shear fatigue data: Implied from tensile data, k = 1
Solution type: Full elastoplastic solution (Solid Mechanics with Plasticity)
tools.notes: Use a Time Dependent or parametric load cycle including loading and unloading so that strain ranges are captured.

tools.name: Morrow (Energy-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Energy-based life model Delta_W_d = W_f' (N_f)^m, relating the dissipated energy density per cycle (plastic, creep, viscoplastic, total or user-defined) to cycles to failure. Useful for thermo-mechanical fatigue of solders and metals where hysteresis energy controls damage; requires Calculate dissipated energy in the material model.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Energy Based > Criterion = Morrow. Java: physics("ftg").create("ener1", "EnergyBasedModel", 3); set("ftgEnerCriterion", "Morrow"); set("ftgEnerType", "Creep" | "Viscoplasticity" | "User"); material group fatigueEnergyMorrow (Wf_Morrow, m_Morrow).

parameters.name: ftgEnerType
parameters.description: Plastic, creep, viscoplastic or total dissipation density, or user defined (with integration order).

parameters.name: Wf_Morrow, m_Morrow
parameters.description: Fatigue energy coefficient and exponent.

tools.notes: The dissipated energy variables (e.g. solid.Wc, solid.Wp) must be stored during the load-cycle simulation.

tools.name: Darveaux (Energy-Based Fatigue)
tools.description: Solder-joint fatigue model that splits life into crack initiation N0 = K1*Delta_W_ave^k2 and crack growth da/dN = K3*Delta_W_ave^k4, with Delta_W_ave the volume-averaged dissipated energy density per cycle (averaged over individual domains or the entire selection) to reduce mesh sensitivity at singular corners. Set a = 0 for initiation only or K1 = 0 for growth only. Domain level only.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Energy Based > Criterion = Darveaux. Java: set("ftgEnerCriterion", "Darveaux"); set("ftgEnerVolAverMethod", "IndividualDomains" | "EntireSelection"); material group fatigueEnergyDarveaux (K1_Darveaux, k2_Darveaux, K3_Darveaux, k4_Darveaux, Wref_Darveaux).

parameters.name: K1, k2, K3, k4
parameters.description: Initiation and growth constants.

parameters.name: Crack size a
parameters.description: Characteristic crack length for failure.

parameters.name: ftgEnerVolAverMethod
parameters.description: Volume averaging per domain or over the whole selection.

tools.notes: Available only on domains in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry.

tools.name: Cumulative Damage (Fatigue)
tools.description: Variable-amplitude fatigue by rainflow cycle counting of the stress history (principal or signed von Mises) into a mean-range matrix, followed by Palmgren-Miner linear damage summation using an S-N curve with R-value dependence, mean-stress dependence or amplitude only (with Gerber/Goodman/Soderberg correction). The history can be the full solution or Generalized loads (unit load cases with weighting coefficient lists for very long histories). Results: usage factor ftg.fus plus counted stress cycles ftg.csc and relative usage ftg.rus at the most damaged point.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Cumulative Damage. Java: physics("ftg").create("cdam1", "CumulativeDamageModel2", 2); set("cDamAnalysisType", "cDamTypeSolution" | "cDamTypeGeneralized"); set("lifeCurve", "int1").

parameters.name: cDamAnalysisType
parameters.description: Solution history or generalized loads.

parameters.name: Nm, Nr
parameters.description: Number of mean-value and range bins for the rainflow matrix (default 10).

parameters.name: S-N curve type, lifeCurve
parameters.description: f_SN(R,N), f_SN(sigma_m,N) or f_SN(N) function.

parameters.name: m, N_cut
parameters.description: Number of block repetitions and cycle cutoff (endurance).

tools.notes: Stresses above the S-N value at 0.1 cycles are reported as static failure. Visualize csc and rus with the Matrix Histogram plot.

tools.name: Harmonic Vibration (Fatigue)
tools.description: Fatigue from a steady-state frequency sweep (sine vibration testing): each excitation frequency contributes damage according to its dwell time or cycle count, a linear or logarithmic sweep rate, and the stress amplitude (directional stress along a vector/coordinate axis, or signed von Mises) evaluated against an S-N curve with Palmgren-Miner summation. The result is a usage factor ftg.fus.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Harmonic Vibration (requires a Frequency Domain load-cycle study). Java: physics("ftg").create("vibr1", "VibrationFatigueModel", 2).

parameters.name: Frequency history
parameters.description: Time duration, Number of cycles, Linear frequency sweep (rate C) or Logarithmic sweep (octave rate).

parameters.name: Stress / Direction
parameters.description: Directional stress (vector or coordinate axis) or Signed von Mises.

parameters.name: S-N curve type
parameters.description: R-value, mean-stress or amplitude dependent S-N curve with mean-stress correction.

tools.notes: Assumes the sweep is slow enough for steady state at every frequency. Base Excitation with a harmonic perturbation typically drives the structural study.

tools.name: Random Vibration (Fatigue)
tools.description: Spectral fatigue for PSD excitation: stress response PSD moments (EVMS equivalent von Mises or a user-defined stress linear in displacement) are computed from a random-vibration reduced-order model between lower and upper frequencies, a cycle counting model (Dirlik for general spectra, Bendat for narrow band) gives the amplitude probability density, and Palmgren-Miner integration against an S-N curve, Basquin or Approximate S-N curve yields usage per unit time ftg.dfus, usage over the duration ftg.fus and life ftg.life.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Random Vibration (after a Random Vibration (PSD) setup). Java: physics("ftg").create("rand1", "RandomFatigueModel", 2); set("cyclecountingmodel", "dirlik" | "bendat").

parameters.name: Random vibration model
parameters.description: ROM with the Random Vibration node (PSDs).

parameters.name: Stress method
parameters.description: Equivalent von Mises stress (EVMS) or user defined linear stress.

parameters.name: f_L, f_U, n_f
parameters.description: Frequency range and discretization for spectral moments.

parameters.name: cyclecountingmodel, t_d, L_cut
parameters.description: Dirlik or Bendat, duration of the random event, life cutoff.

tools.notes: Mean stresses are not considered. Changing the shell through-thickness location requires recomputing the Model Reduction step.

tools.name: Mean Stress Correction: Goodman, Gerber, Soderberg and Morrow (Fatigue)
tools.description: Methods to include mean stress when the S-N data are for fully reversed loading: Goodman (linear interaction with ultimate strength), Gerber (parabolic interaction with ultimate strength), Soderberg (linear with yield stress, most conservative) in Stress Life, Harmonic Vibration and Cumulative Damage; Morrow in the combined Basquin-Coffin-Manson and Wang-Brown strain models. Alternatively, S-N curves with explicit R-ratio or mean-stress dependence can be supplied.
tools.usage: Fatigue > Stress Life / Cumulative Damage / Harmonic Vibration > Mean Stress Correction > Method = None | Gerber | Goodman | Soderberg; Strain Life (combined) or Strain Based (Wang-Brown) > Mean stress correction = Morrow.

parameters.name: sigma_u
parameters.description: Ultimate tensile strength for Gerber and Goodman.

parameters.name: sigma_ys
parameters.description: Yield stress for Soderberg.

tools.example: Fatigue > Stress Life 1 > Mean Stress Correction: Method = Goodman, sigma_u = 600[MPa]
tools.notes: Random vibration fatigue ignores mean stresses.

tools.name: Fatigue Result Variables and Matrix Histogram
tools.description: Fatigue results are fields of the Fatigue interface: ftg.ctf (cycles to failure, stress-/strain-/energy-life models, plot on log scale), ftg.fus (fatigue usage factor for stress-based, cumulative damage, harmonic and random vibration; fus < 1 means no fatigue), ftg.dfus and ftg.life (random vibration), and ftg.csc / ftg.rus (counted stress cycles and relative usage at the worst point of a cumulative-damage evaluation). The Matrix Histogram 2D plot shows rainflow cycle and damage distributions over mean stress and range.
tools.usage: Results > 3D Plot Group > Surface/Volume with expr ftg.fus or log10(ftg.ctf); Results > 2D Plot Group > Matrix Histogram (Java type MatrixHistogram) with ftg.csc or ftg.rus.

parameters.name: ftg.ctf
parameters.description: Number of cycles to failure (limited by the cycle cutoff).

parameters.name: ftg.fus
parameters.description: Fatigue usage factor (reciprocal of a safety factor for linear criteria).

parameters.name: ftg.csc, ftg.rus
parameters.description: Rainflow counted cycles and relative usage per bin.

parameters.name: ftg.dfus, ftg.life
parameters.description: Usage per unit time and life in random vibration.

tools.notes: Variable names are prefixed by the Fatigue interface tag (ftg by default). Application Library: Fatigue_Module/Damage/frame_with_cutout shows the Matrix Histogram.

tools.name: Solid Rotor, Fixed Frame (srotf)
tools.description: 3D solid rotor interface with equations formulated in a space-fixed frame (frame acceleration forces from rotation included automatically), so eigenfrequencies, whirl and Campbell diagrams are directly in the fixed frame and easier to interpret than with Solid Rotor (corotating frame). It assumes an axially symmetric rotor, while bearings and foundations may be anisotropic; the same bearing, foundation, seal and coupling features as Solid Rotor are available.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Rotordynamics > Solid Rotor, Fixed Frame. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("srotf", "SolidRotorFixedFrame", "geom1"); features RotatingFrame (rotf), JournalBearing (jrb), FixAxRot (far).

parameters.name: Rotating Frame
parameters.description: Rotor axis and speed (replaces Change Rotor Speed for solid rotors in 6.4).

parameters.name: Bearings and foundations
parameters.description: Journal, Thrust, Radial Roller, Active Magnetic, Multi-Spool bearings; Flexible/Moving foundation; Squeeze-Film Damper.

parameters.name: Fixed Axial Rotation
parameters.description: Reference cross section for torsion.

tools.notes: Not valid for non-axisymmetric rotors such as crankshafts; use Solid Rotor there. See the existing Solid Rotor (rotsld) / Beam Rotor (rotbm) entry.

tools.name: Rotating Frame (Solid Rotor)
tools.description: Defines the rotor axis (x/y/z axis or through selected points) and rotational speed of a Solid Rotor or Solid Rotor, Fixed Frame domain, generating centrifugal, Coriolis and spin-softening effects in the rotating formulation. In 6.4 it supersedes Change Rotor Speed for solid rotors, so multi-rotor systems at different speeds (geared rotors) use several Rotating Frame nodes.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor > Domains > Rotating Frame. Java: physics("rotsld").feature("rotf1").set("axisOfRotation", "xAxis" | "pointSelection"); set("speedInput", "RPT" | "RPTConst").

parameters.name: axisOfRotation
parameters.description: Coordinate axis or axis through selected points.

parameters.name: speedInput
parameters.description: Revolutions per time or angular velocity input (constant or time dependent).

tools.notes: In Beam Rotor the speed is set on the interface (Rotor Speed section, variable omegar) and per-edge with Change Rotor Speed.

tools.name: Journal Bearing (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Radial bearing support on a cylindrical journal surface (Solid Rotor) or a point (Beam Rotor). Bearing models: No clearance (rigid), Cylindrical (plain) hydrodynamic with viscosity, clearance and length using the short-bearing Reynolds solution, Total spring and damping constant (with optional translation-rotation coupling), Total force and moment as functions of journal motion, and Force per reference area. Foundation properties can be Fixed, Flexible, Moving or a Squeeze-film damper, and a Misalignment subnode is allowed when clearance exists.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor > Journal Bearing. Java: physics("rotbm").create("jrb1", "JournalBearing", 0); set("BearingModel", "NoClearance" | "PlainHydrodynamic" | "kTot"); set("C", ...); set("L", ...); set("mure", ...).

parameters.name: Bearing orientation
parameters.description: Orientation vector for the local x (solid) or y (beam) direction and rotation about the axis.

parameters.name: BearingModel
parameters.description: NoClearance, PlainHydrodynamic (C, L, mure), kTot (k_u, k_theta, c_u, c_theta, couplings), total force/moment, force per area.

parameters.name: Foundation properties
parameters.description: Fixed, Flexible (Flexible Foundation), Moving (Moving Foundation) or Squeeze-film damper.

tools.notes: For a full Reynolds-equation film use the Hydrodynamic Bearing interface with a rotor-bearing coupling.

tools.name: Thrust Bearing (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Axial bearing acting on a circular rotor cross section (collar) with models No clearance, Total spring and damping constant (axial and bending stiffness/damping, optional coupling), Total force and moment, or Force per reference area. Like journal bearings it supports flexible or moving foundations and misalignment.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor > Thrust Bearing. Java: physics("rotsld").create("thrb1", "ThrustBearing", 2).

parameters.name: BearingModel
parameters.description: No clearance, total spring and damping constant, total force and moment, force per reference area.

parameters.name: k_u, k_theta, c_u, c_theta
parameters.description: Axial and bending stiffness and damping (defaults for rotational terms from Euler tensor of the collar).

parameters.name: Foundation properties
parameters.description: Fixed, Flexible or Moving foundation subnodes.

tools.notes: Hydrodynamic thrust bearings (tilting pad, tapered, step) are modeled in the Hydrodynamic Bearing interface.

tools.name: Radial Roller Bearing (Rotordynamics and Multibody Dynamics)
tools.description: Rolling-element bearing whose element forces are computed from Hertz contact theory, including clearance and nonlinear stiffness: Deep groove, Angular contact, Self-aligning ball bearings, Spherical, Cylindrical and Tapered roller bearings (single or double row) with ball/roller count and diameter, pitch diameter, race contour radii and contact angle. Roller force distributions are available as variables such as rotsld.rrb1.fbx. It supports flexible/moving foundations, squeeze-film dampers and misalignment.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor / Multibody Dynamics > Radial Roller Bearing. Java: physics("mbd").create("rrb1", "RadialRollerBearing", 2); physics("rotbm").create("rrb1", "RadialRollerBearing", 0).

parameters.name: Bearing Type
parameters.description: Deep groove, angular contact, self aligning ball; spherical, cylindrical, tapered roller.

parameters.name: Geometric properties
parameters.description: Rows, number of balls/rollers, diameters, pitch diameter, race contour radii, contact angle, clearance.

parameters.name: Foundation, Misalignment subnodes
parameters.description: Flexible/Moving Foundation, Squeeze-Film Damper, Misalignment.

tools.notes: Strongly nonlinear: use time-dependent analysis for rattling and nonsynchronous vibration; linearized stiffness is used in eigenfrequency studies.

tools.name: Active Magnetic Bearing (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Radial magnetic bearing with a PID feedback controller setting coil currents from the measured journal displacement. Transient analysis uses the nonlinear force-current-displacement law; stationary analysis uses proportional control with linearized forces; frequency-domain and eigenfrequency analyses use a linearized, frequency-dependent effective impedance. Inputs are air gap, controller gains Kp, Ki, Kd, force constant and bias currents in the local lateral directions.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Solid Rotor, Fixed Frame / Beam Rotor > Active Magnetic Bearing.

parameters.name: Air gap h
parameters.description: Nominal gap in local lateral directions.

parameters.name: Kp, Ki, Kd, Fc
parameters.description: Proportional, integral and derivative gains and force constant.

parameters.name: Bias currents
parameters.description: Currents supporting static load (equal +/- bias gives no static capacity).

tools.example:
Beam Rotor > Active Magnetic Bearing 1 at point 3
Air gap 0.5[mm], Kp = 5e3[A/m], Ki = 1e4[A/(m*s)], Kd = 5[A*s/m], bias currents (2, 1)[A]
Study: Eigenfrequency with rotor speed sweep -> Campbell diagram
tools.notes: Supports Flexible, Moving and squeeze-film foundations like other bearings.

tools.name: Flexible and Moving Foundation (Rotordynamics Bearings)
tools.description: Subnodes created automatically when a bearing's Foundation properties are Flexible or Moving. Flexible Foundation adds translational and rotational stiffness and damping (with optional coupling terms) between bearing and ground, representing pedestals and casings. Moving Foundation prescribes foundation displacement and rotation at the bearing center, e.g. for base excitation of vehicle or seismic loads on rotors.
tools.usage: <Journal/Thrust/Radial Roller/Active Magnetic Bearing> > Foundation properties = Flexible | Moving (subnode added automatically). Java subnode types: FlexibleFoundation (ffd; keys k_u, k_th, k_uth, k_thu, c_u, c_th, c_uth, c_thu as 3x3 matrices), MovingFoundation (mfd).

parameters.name: k_u, k_theta, c_u, c_theta (+ coupling)
parameters.description: Foundation stiffness and damping (Flexible).

parameters.name: u_f, theta_f
parameters.description: Prescribed foundation displacement and rotation (Moving).

tools.notes: These subnodes cannot be added or removed manually. The same subnodes are used by Radial Roller Bearing in Multibody Dynamics.

tools.name: Squeeze-Film Damper (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Bearing foundation option that adds an oil squeeze-film damper between the bearing outer race and the housing, with damping coefficients from a short-bearing approximation (viscosity, clearance, length) and a centering spring (stiffness and damping) to carry static load. In the Hydrodynamic Bearing interface a full Reynolds-equation Squeeze-Film Damper node is also available.
tools.usage: <Journal/Radial Roller/Active Magnetic Bearing> > Foundation properties = Squeeze-film damper (subnode type SqueezeFilmDamper, tag sfd); Hydrodynamic Bearing > Squeeze-Film Damper.

parameters.name: mu, C, L
parameters.description: Lubricant viscosity, damper clearance and length.

parameters.name: k_cs, c_cs
parameters.description: Centering spring stiffness and damping.

tools.notes: Common in aero engines to reduce vibration amplitudes when passing critical speeds.

tools.name: Misalignment (Rotordynamics Bearings)
tools.description: Subnode of bearings and Rotor Coupling that prescribes parallel (u0) and angular (theta0) misalignment. For stiffness-based bearings it acts like a spring predeformation; for hydrodynamic bearings it changes the film thickness distribution and hence pressure. Used to study 2x vibration signatures, bearing loads and coupling forces from misaligned shafts.
tools.usage: <Journal/Thrust/Radial Roller Bearing, Rotor Coupling, Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing> > Misalignment. Java: feature("rrb1").create("mlgn1", "Misalignment", 2).

parameters.name: u0 (parallel)
parameters.description: Lateral offsets (x,y for solid rotors; y,z for beam rotors and hydrodynamic bearings).

parameters.name: theta0 (angular)
parameters.description: Angular misalignment components.

tools.notes: Not allowed under Journal/Thrust Bearing with the No clearance model.

tools.name: Multi-Spool Bearing (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Intershaft bearing between two coaxial rotors running at different speeds (e.g. low- and high-pressure spools of a jet engine), connecting the journal on one shaft to the bushing surface on the other with rigid or flexible translational and rotational stiffness and damping.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor > Multi-Spool Bearing (Boundary/Point Selection = journal on one shaft; Destination selection = other shaft). Java: physics("rotbm").create("msb1", "MultiSpoolBearing", 0).

parameters.name: Displacement connection
parameters.description: Rigid or Flexible (translational stiffness/damping).

parameters.name: Rotational connection
parameters.description: Stiffness/damping for tilting.

parameters.name: Bearing orientation
parameters.description: Local axes definition.

tools.notes: Each rotor's speed is set with Change Rotor Speed (Beam Rotor) or separate Rotating Frame nodes (solid rotors).

tools.name: Liquid Annular Seal (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Adds rotordynamic stiffness, damping and added-mass coefficients generated by the flow through annular liquid seals (pump wear rings, balance pistons). Seal models: Black and Jenssen (finite-length seals without inlet swirl) and Childs (short seals with inlet swirl). Inputs include radius, seal length, clearance, fluid viscosity and density and flow data (pressure drop, entrance loss, swirl).
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor > Liquid Annular Seal. Java: physics("rotbm").create("las1", "LiquidAnnularSeal", 0); set("SealModel", "Black" | "Childs"); set("Ls", ...); set("C", ...); set("dP", ...).

parameters.name: SealModel
parameters.description: Black (Black and Jenssen) or Childs.

parameters.name: R, Ls, C
parameters.description: Radial distance, seal length, seal clearance.

parameters.name: mu, rho, dP
parameters.description: Fluid viscosity, density and pressure drop across the seal.

tools.notes: Cross-coupled seal stiffness can destabilize rotors; check with a Stability Diagram.

tools.name: Rotor Coupling (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Connects two rotor segments at a cross section: Spline (displacement and axial rotation coupled, tilting free), Torsional (displacement and tilt coupled, axial rotation through a torsional spring) or User defined (rigid/flexible displacement, axial rotation and tilting connections with stiffness). On exterior boundaries the other side is treated as fixed. Supports misalignment.
tools.usage: Solid Rotor / Beam Rotor > Rotor Coupling. Java: physics("rotbm").create("cpl1", "RotorCoupling", 0).

parameters.name: Coupling type
parameters.description: Spline, Torsional (k_theta,ax) or User defined.

parameters.name: k_u, k_theta,ax, tilting stiffness
parameters.description: Connection stiffnesses for flexible connections.

tools.notes: Add Misalignment for misaligned couplings.

tools.name: Disk (Beam Rotor)
tools.description: Point feature that adds the inertia of rotating components (impellers, disks, pulleys, couplings) to a Beam Rotor, including gyroscopic effects. The disk is Circular (mass with polar and diametral moments, or geometric density/diameter/thickness) or Noncircular (full inertia tensor), and its center of mass can be at the point, offset (radial, angular, axial offsets creating unbalance forces that rotate with the rotor) or user defined.
tools.usage: Beam Rotor > Points > Disk. Java: physics("rotbm").create("disk1", "Disk", 0); set("COM", "SelectedPoints" | "Relative"); set("SpecifiedBy", "Inertia" | "GeomDim"); set("mass", ...); set("Ip", ...); set("Id", ...).

parameters.name: COM
parameters.description: Center of mass at selected points, offset (radial zr, angle, axial za) or user defined.

parameters.name: SpecifiedBy
parameters.description: Inertia (mass, Ip, Id) or GeomDim (rho, d, h).

parameters.name: Icg
parameters.description: Full inertia tensor for noncircular disks.

tools.notes: Eccentric disks give synchronous unbalance response, phase shifted in frequency-domain studies.

tools.name: Rotor Cross Section (Beam Rotor)
tools.description: Required Beam Rotor node for the shaft section: Circular (diameter), Pipe (outer and inner diameter) or User defined (area, area moments, polar moment, shear flexibility, stress evaluation points), plus the orientation vector of the local y axis. Timoshenko beam theory with shear deformation is used, so rather thick shafts are handled accurately.
tools.usage: Beam Rotor > Rotor Cross Section (default). Java: physics("rotbm").feature("rcs1").set("SectionType", "CircularSection" | "PipeSection"); set("do_circ", "d_shaft").

parameters.name: SectionType
parameters.description: CircularSection, PipeSection or user defined.

parameters.name: do_circ / do_pipe, di_pipe
parameters.description: Diameters.

parameters.name: Section orientation
parameters.description: Orientation vector for local y.

tools.notes: Stepped shafts are modeled with several edges and cross-section nodes.

tools.name: Rotor Rub (Beam Rotor)
tools.description: Point or edge contact between the rotor and a surrounding stator/housing with a given radial clearance, using penalty or augmented Lagrangian contact and optional Coulomb friction with an effective friction radius. It captures rub-impact phenomena, backward whirl and chaotic motion; strongly nonlinear, so only meaningful in time-dependent analysis.
tools.usage: Beam Rotor > Points (or Edges) > Rotor Rub.

parameters.name: C_rad
parameters.description: Radial clearance between rotor and housing.

parameters.name: Contact method, k_p
parameters.description: Penalty or Augmented Lagrangian with penalty factor.

parameters.name: Include friction, mu_f, R_eff
parameters.description: Friction coefficient and effective radius for the friction moment.

tools.example:
Beam Rotor > Rotor Rub 1 at the seal location: C_rad = 0.2[mm], Penalty, k_p = 1e8[N/m], friction mu_f = 0.1, R_eff = 30[mm]
Study: Time Dependent run-up
tools.notes: Requires small time steps near impacts.

tools.name: Fixed Axial Rotation and Change Rotor Speed (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Fixed Axial Rotation is the default node that selects a cross section (or point) as reference for the axial (torsional) rotation relative to the rigid rotation, removing the torsional rigid-body mode. Change Rotor Speed assigns a different speed to selected Beam Rotor edges than the interface default, for geared or multi-shaft systems; from 6.4 it is not available in solid rotors, where Rotating Frame is used instead.
tools.usage: Beam Rotor/Solid Rotor > Fixed Axial Rotation (default); Beam Rotor > Edges > More > Change Rotor Speed. Java: physics("rotbm").feature("far1"); physics("rotbm").create("rsp1", "RotorSpeed", 1).

parameters.name: Fixed Axial Rotation selection
parameters.description: Reference cross section/point; only present when torsion is included (No torsion cleared in Beam Rotor).

parameters.name: Change Rotor Speed
parameters.description: Revolutions per time or angular velocity for the selected edges.

tools.notes: Beam Rotor includes torsion/axial vibration only if No torsion / No axial vibration are cleared in the interface.

tools.name: Hydrodynamic Bearing (hdb)
tools.description: Thin-film lubrication interface on 3D surfaces that solves the Reynolds equation (with optional gas flow, cavitation, turbulence corrections and asperity contact) for the pressure in journal bearings, thrust bearings, floating ring bearings and squeeze-film dampers. It can be used standalone to compute bearing loads and dynamic coefficients, or coupled to Solid Rotor, Beam Rotor, Solid Mechanics or Multibody Dynamics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Rotordynamics > Hydrodynamic Bearing. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("hdb", "HydrodynamicBearing", "geom1"); features HydrodynamicJournalBearing (hjb), HydrodynamicThrustBearing (htb), FloatingRingBearing (frb), SqueezeFilmDamper (sfd), BearingOrientation (bax), Border (bdr), Inlet (inl).

parameters.name: Bearing features
parameters.description: Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing, Floating Ring Bearing, Hydrodynamic Thrust Bearing, Squeeze-Film Damper.

parameters.name: Border / Inlet / Outlet / Symmetry
parameters.description: Film boundary conditions (ambient, supply pressure, symmetry).

parameters.name: Bearing Orientation
parameters.description: Bearing axis (bearingAxis = xAxis/yAxis/zAxis).

tools.notes: Journal and bearing surfaces are not in the geometry; the film is represented on a reference surface. Requires the Rotordynamics Module.

tools.name: Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing (Hydrodynamic Bearing)
tools.description: Fluid-film journal bearing with built-in film geometries: Cylindrical (plain), Elliptical, Split halves, Multilobe (preload factor or pad offset, number of pads), Tilting pad (pad clearance, radius, tilt angle, pivot offset) or User defined film thickness. Journal motion is given as displacement, eccentricity and direction, or external load, with speed as angular speed, revolutions per time or a velocity field from a coupled rotor; lubricant viscosity and density may be pressure/temperature dependent.
tools.usage: Hydrodynamic Bearing > Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing (default node). Java: feature("hjb1").set("BearingType", "Plain" | "Elliptic" | "SplitHalves" | "Multilobe"); set("Specify", "Displacement" | "Load"); set("JournalVelocity", "AngSpeed" | "RevolutionsPerTime" | "VelField"); set("mure", ...).

parameters.name: BearingType
parameters.description: Plain, Elliptic, SplitHalves, Multilobe, tilting pad or user defined.

parameters.name: C_plain / C_multi, PreLoadFactor_*, N
parameters.description: Clearances, preload factor (specify or compute from offset) and number of pads.

parameters.name: Specify
parameters.description: Journal displacement, eccentricity/direction or load.

parameters.name: mure, rho
parameters.description: Lubricant viscosity and density.

tools.notes: Foundation subnodes (Flexible/Moving/Squeeze-film) and Misalignment are available. Elastohydrodynamic bearings couple to Solid Mechanics with Solid-Bearing Coupling (elastohydrodynamic_journal_bearing).

tools.name: Floating Ring Bearing (Hydrodynamic Bearing)
tools.description: Bearing with a free ring between journal and housing, giving inner and outer oil films in series (turbochargers). The ring is Full floating (rotates under viscous drag) or Semi floating (no axial rotation), with position/orientation computed from momentum balance (ring mass and inertia) or user defined; Inner Film Properties, Outer Film Properties and Inner-Outer Film Connection subnodes describe the films.
tools.usage: Hydrodynamic Bearing > Floating Ring Bearing (subnodes InnerFilmProperties, OuterFilmProperties, InnerOuterFilmConnection). Java: physics("hdb").create("frb1", "FloatingRingBearing", 2).

parameters.name: Ring type
parameters.description: Full floating or Semi floating.

parameters.name: m_ring, I_ring, I_p,ring
parameters.description: Ring mass and inertias for automatic motion.

parameters.name: Ring speed
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined ring-to-journal speed ratio.

tools.notes: Often combined with a Beam Rotor through Beam Rotor-Bearing Coupling for run-up transients.

tools.name: Hydrodynamic Thrust Bearing (Hydrodynamic Bearing)
tools.description: Fluid-film thrust bearing on a collar surface with built-in pad geometries: Tilting pad (number of pads, pad arc, inner/outer diameter, optional pad inertia, groove depth), Tapered (taper with constant-width or constant-arc grooves), Step (step height, film thickness on pad) or User defined clearance as a function of polar coordinates.
tools.usage: Hydrodynamic Bearing > Hydrodynamic Thrust Bearing. Java: physics("hdb").create("htb1", "HydrodynamicThrustBearing", 2); set("BearingType", "StepBearing" | "UserDef"); set("GrooveType", "ConstantArc" | "ConstantWidth").

parameters.name: BearingType
parameters.description: Tilting pad, tapered, StepBearing or UserDef.

parameters.name: N, gamma_p, d_i, d_o
parameters.description: Pad count, pad arc and diameters.

parameters.name: hB1 / h_film, h_s, h_g
parameters.description: Film thickness, step height, groove depth.

tools.notes: Flexible/Moving Foundation subnodes are available.

tools.name: Rotor-Bearing Couplings: Solid Rotor, Beam Rotor and Solid-Bearing (multiphysics couplings)
tools.description: Couplings that let the Reynolds-equation film act on structural models: Solid Rotor-Bearing Coupling (Solid Rotor with Hydrodynamic Bearing interface), Beam Rotor-Bearing Coupling (Beam Rotor with Hydrodynamic Bearing) and Solid-Bearing Coupling (Solid Mechanics or Multibody Dynamics, optionally including foundation motion). Rotor displacement/velocity sets the film thickness and the film pressure loads the rotor, enabling nonlinear run-up transients and elastohydrodynamic analyses.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Rotordynamics > Solid Rotor with Hydrodynamic Bearing | Beam Rotor with Hydrodynamic Bearing; or Multiphysics > Solid-Bearing Coupling. Java: multiphysics().create("srbc1", "SolidRotorBearingCoupling", 2); multiphysics().create("brbc1", "BeamRotorBearingCoupling", 2); multiphysics().create("sbco1", "SolidBearingCoupling", 2).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Rotor/solid interface and Hydrodynamic Bearing interface.

parameters.name: Include foundation (Solid-Bearing)
parameters.description: Foundation boundaries whose motion modifies the film.

tools.notes: For linear analyses, dynamic bearing coefficients can replace the full coupling (Total spring and damping constant).

tools.name: Bearing Dynamic Coefficients (Hydrodynamic Bearing)
tools.description: Linearized stiffness and damping coefficients (Kxx, Kxy, Kyx, Kyy, Cxx...) of a fluid-film bearing about the static equilibrium position for a given load, computed in the Rotordynamics Module by infinitesimal perturbation of the Reynolds equation (pressure-perturbation DOFs). They feed linear rotordynamic eigenvalue and stability analyses, together with critical journal mass and critical whirl speed; finite perturbation is demonstrated as an alternative.
tools.usage: Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing with Specify = Load; evaluate the dynamic coefficient variables after a stationary equilibrium solution.

parameters.name: Static load
parameters.description: External load defining the equilibrium eccentricity.

parameters.name: Perturbation method
parameters.description: Infinitesimal (built in) or finite perturbation (manual).

tools.notes: Valid only when dynamic loads are small compared to the static load; lightly loaded bearings need nonlinear transient analysis.

tools.name: Campbell Diagram and Critical Speeds (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Result template (Solid Rotor, Solid Rotor Fixed Frame, Beam Rotor) plotting eigenfrequencies versus rotor speed from an Eigenfrequency study with a parametric sweep of speed, with a Color Expression marking backward (purple), straight-line (green) and forward (red) whirl. Critical speeds are the intersections with the omega = Omega line in the fixed frame; for Solid Rotor (corotating frame) forward-whirl frequencies are shifted by +Omega and backward by -Omega, and auxiliary lines can be selected in the interface settings.
tools.usage: Study: Eigenfrequency + Parametric Sweep of the rotor speed parameter; Results > Add Result Template > Campbell Diagram (1D Global plot with Color Expression and Graph Markers for intersections).

parameters.name: Rotor speed sweep
parameters.description: Parameter used in the interface rotor speed.

parameters.name: Auxiliary lines
parameters.description: Selected in the rotor interface Result Settings (e.g. 1x, 2x speed lines).

parameters.name: Whirl variables
parameters.description: Forward/backward natural frequency variables and <phys>.i_sd for coloring.

tools.notes: Campbell diagrams ignore bearing nonlinearity and speed-dependent excitation phase; confirm with unbalance response or transients.

tools.name: Whirl Plot and Whirl Direction (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: The Whirl plot draws rotor mode shapes swept through a full phase cycle as orbits along the rotor axis (planes and rings with tube radius), visualizing forward or backward whirl. The shape and directivity index <phys>.i_sd (e.g. rotbm.i_sd) classifies each point: -1 backward circular, between -1 and 0 backward elliptical, 0 straight line, between 0 and 1 forward elliptical, +1 forward circular.
tools.usage: Results > 3D Plot Group > More Line Plots > Whirl (Java type Whirl); evaluate rotbm.i_sd or rotsld.i_sd in plots or Color Expressions.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Rotor edges to draw.

parameters.name: Number of planes / rings, Tube radius
parameters.description: Visualization of orbits.

parameters.name: <phys>.i_sd
parameters.description: Shape and directivity index for whirl classification.

tools.notes: At nodes of a mode shape i_sd is undefined. The Whirl plot requires the Rotordynamics Module.

tools.name: Stability Diagram (Rotordynamics)
tools.description: Result template plotting the modal damping ratio versus rotor speed from an eigenfrequency sweep; a negative damping ratio (eigenvalue with negative imaginary part) indicates instability, and the first zero crossing is the stability threshold (onset of instability), typical for oil whirl/whip in hydrodynamic bearings and destabilizing seals. A Color Expression shows stable (green) and unstable (red) modes, with an intermediate band of +-1e-5 treated as undamped.
tools.usage: Results > Add Result Template > <rotor interface> > Stability Diagram (after an Eigenfrequency study swept over speed).

parameters.name: Damping ratio
parameters.description: Derived from complex eigenfrequencies.

parameters.name: Intermediate interval
parameters.description: Default zeta in [-1e-5, 1e-5] considered undamped.

tools.notes: Complements the Campbell diagram, which shows frequencies but not damping.

tools.name: Transient with FFT (Rotordynamics study)
tools.description: Rotordynamics study that runs a Time Dependent analysis followed by a Time to Frequency FFT for each rotor speed in a parametric sweep, producing data for waterfall diagrams (frequency spectra versus speed) that reveal subsynchronous whirl, rubbing and nonlinear bearing effects. It is inexpensive with Beam Rotor but very costly with Solid Rotor.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies > Transient with FFT (Time Dependent + Time to Frequency FFT with parametric sweep); Results > Waterfall plot. Java study steps: create("time", "Transient"); create("tffft", "TimeToFreqFFT").

parameters.name: Parametric sweep
parameters.description: Rotor angular speed values.

parameters.name: Time range
parameters.description: Long enough to reach steady state for the FFT window.

parameters.name: FFT settings
parameters.description: Window, frequency range in the Time to Frequency FFT step.

tools.notes: See the existing Time to Frequency FFT entry for FFT settings.
